references.text: The preceding context regarding lending and keeping another's property, which establishes the principles for compensation when the owner is not present.
The continuation of laws concerning compensation, here linked to the seduction of a virgin, illustrating the broader principle of restitution.
The command to pay a worker's wages on the same day, addressing the theme of fair payment for hire and labor.
Laws requiring that a hired worker's wages be paid at the proper time, expanding on the principle of hired labor mentioned in the verse.
Laws concerning Hebrew servants and their service, relating to the concept of hired work and ownership.
Both verses clarify the principle that natural loss or the owner's presence exempts the borrower from liability for compensation.
